summary: Proof of concept E0b (experiments v06, proposal r22, H8) on synthetic bags, Kaggle CPU, full declared scale; it replaces E0 (Results/poc_e0.*), whose verdicts were early-stopping artifacts. Gate 0 passed (1.1952 vs 1.2642). At the primary rho = 1, P1 is supported, P2 is partially supported (the surrogate recovers the prior, P2c, and its error falls, P2b, but SS^w does not improve over the untargeted arm, P2a), and P4 is supported, so H8 is not carried forward under the pre-registered rule. Recovery rises with rho (mean per-item Spearman of the full model 0.00, 0.05, 0.14, 0.32 at rho 0, 0.5, 1, 2) and only at rho 2 does the full model clearly beat the untargeted arm on SS^w (0.242 vs 0.125, descriptive). P3 at rho 1: -0.156 [-0.193, -0.125].

metrics.name: SS^w (Ec. 93) on test bags
metrics.why: Primary endpoint of H5 and the score H8 reads against the untargeted arm.

metrics.name: Normalized surrogate error ||Rhat_c - Rc||_F^2 / (8 N_b vbar) on test bags (1 = zero predictor)
metrics.why: The quantity the normalized Ec. 77 penalty minimizes.

metrics.name: Mean per-item Spearman of Rhat_c vs Rc over test segments
metrics.why: Prior recovery; a lower error alone can come from shrinkage toward a low-variance prior.

metrics.name: Subject-level AUROC of the summed item profile

hypotheses.statement: The full model has a class-weighted skill score above zero at rho = 1.
hypotheses.test: One-sample Wilcoxon (greater), seed as unit, n = 10, Holm over P1, P2a, P2b, P2c
hypotheses.rationale: Adjusted p well below alpha; models were trained (median best epoch 14), unlike E0.

hypotheses.statement: At rho = 1 the full model has a higher SS^w, a lower normalized surrogate error and a higher mean per-item Spearman than the untargeted arm.
hypotheses.metric: SS^w; normalized surrogate error; mean per-item Spearman
hypotheses.test: Three paired Wilcoxon tests (P2a, P2b, P2c), Holm over the four tests
hypotheses.criterion: Supported when P2a, P2b and P2c all pass; partially supported when one or two pass.
hypotheses.observed: P2a: diff +0.0047, adjusted p 0.3477, CI [-0.0194, 0.0296]. P2b: 1.013 vs 62.88, adjusted p 0.0039, rank-biserial 1.0. P2c: 0.139 vs 0.021, diff 0.118 [0.0995, 0.1366], adjusted p 0.0039, rank-biserial 1.0.
hypotheses.rationale: The penalty makes the surrogate recover the prior (P2c, all ten seeds) and keeps its error near the zero predictor while the untargeted surrogate drifts to 60x; but at rho 1 that recovery (Spearman 0.14) does not translate into a better item profile (P2a). At rho 2 (Spearman 0.32) the full model's SS^w is about double the untargeted arm's, which is descriptive only.

hypotheses.statement: At rho = 0 the bootstrap interval of the paired SS^w difference full - untargeted contains zero.
hypotheses.test: Percentile bootstrap (B = 10000) of the seed-mean paired difference
hypotheses.criterion: Supported when the interval contains zero.
hypotheses.observed: Diff -0.0000, CI [-0.0093, 0.0090]; full Spearman -0.004 at rho 0.
hypotheses.rationale: No gain and no recovery when the audio carries no prior; absence of evidence with n = 10.

novelty.claim: Distilling the interviewer-prompt prior into acoustics, with text as training-only privileged information (pillar C3, r22), improves the item profile over the same model without the penalty and does nothing when the audio does not carry the prior.
novelty.rationale: The distillation mechanism is shown: the penalty recovers the prompt prior from audio when it is there, in proportion to its strength, and not otherwise (P2c, dose response, P4). The claimed benefit on the item profile is not shown at the primary strength (P2a fails) and appears only at the strongest one, descriptively; so the mechanism is justified, the benefit is not.

qualitative_not_applicable: The per-item fidelity heatmap was not rendered as a figure; its numbers are in poc_e0b.json (arms.*.spearman). Dose response of the full model's mean per-item Spearman: 0.00 (rho 0), 0.05 (0.5), 0.14 (1), 0.32 (2); untargeted: 0.00, 0.00, 0.02, 0.17.
limitations: Synthetic bags only; nothing here transfers to E-DAIC.
Recovery at the primary strength is modest (Spearman 0.14 against an oracle 0.52); the SS^w benefit appears only at rho 2, which was not the pre-registered primary reading.
Two pipeline-timing runs (seed 0, rho 1) showed test metrics before launch; no design choice changed after them.
The run took about 6.5 h on Kaggle CPU against a 2 h estimate.
Figures (curves, heatmap, intervals) were not rendered.
next_steps: Operator decision: H8 is not carried forward under the pre-registered rule; decide whether E-DAIC proceeds with the surrogate arms (mechanism shown, benefit only at strong signal) or only with the r12/text arms.
Align E1-E9 with r22 in a later experiments revision.
Render the pre-registered figures from poc_e0b.json.

contribution_type.why: E0b-P1 and E0b-P4 are supported and E0b-P2 is partially supported: the training-only distillation recovers the prior on synthetic bags (P2c) but improves the item profile only at strong signal, so the idea is shown feasible at pilot scale with its benefit unproven.

General.why: No real-data result and no SS^w gain at the primary strength.

Theory.why: No formal result; empirical existence check only.

Use-Inspired.why: Motivated by depression screening, but no E-DAIC evidence yet.

Concept & Feasibility.why: Mechanism shown on synthetic bags with a dose response and a clean negative control (P2c, P4).

Negative Results.why: P2a fails at the primary strength, a partial negative, but the central mechanism test passes.
